> **Supplementary example.** This is a common-source outbreak: its epicurve
> reflects exposure timing and the incubation period rather than transmission,
> so the GMITS growth coefficient here describes the curve shape only. The main
> real-data evaluation of GMITS uses the 2022 England mpox outbreak — see the
> [GMITS research overview](GMITS_Research.html).

# Synthetic Validation

Validates that GMITS recovers known parameters from noise-free,
irregularly spaced data. A 2 × 2 design crosses direction (growth,
a < 0; decay, a > 0) with speed (|a| = 0.3 or 0.4 per day), holding
b, the first value and the time grid fixed, so that the effects of
direction and speed can be read separately. The same four series are
also fitted on an equally spaced grid with the same mean interval.

```{r synth-validate}
# Generate x0 from the ODE solution with known (a, b, x0[1])
synth_series <- function(a, b, x0_1, t_pts) {
  x1 <- (x0_1 - b / a) * exp(-a * t_pts) + b / a
  c(x0_1, diff(x1) / diff(t_pts))
}

t_irr     <- c(0, 2, 4, 7, 10)   # irregular gaps: 2, 2, 3, 3
t_eq      <- seq(0, 10, by = 2.5) # equal gaps, same mean interval
n_ahead_s <- 3
b_s       <- 5
x0_1_s    <- 8

# 2 x 2 design: direction (growth / decay) x speed (|a| = 0.3 / 0.4),
# with b, x0[1] and the time grid held fixed
synth_scen <- expand_grid(
  direction = c("Growth", "Decay"),
  abs_a = c(0.3, 0.4)
) |>
  mutate(a = if_else(direction == "Growth", -abs_a, abs_a))

fit_synth <- function(a, t_fit) {
  dt_mean <- mean(diff(t_fit))
  t_all <- c(t_fit, max(t_fit) + dt_mean * seq_len(n_ahead_s))
  x0 <- synth_series(a, b_s, x0_1_s, t_fit)
  r <- gmits(x0, as.Date("2024-01-01") + t_fit, n_ahead = n_ahead_s)
  list(
    a_hat = r$a,
    traj = tibble(
      t = t_all,
      True = synth_series(a, b_s, x0_1_s, t_all),
      Fitted = c(r$x0_hat, r$x0_future),
      Forecast = rep(c(FALSE, TRUE), c(length(t_fit), n_ahead_s))
    )
  )
}

synth_res <- synth_scen |>
  mutate(
    irr = map(a, fit_synth, t_fit = t_irr),
    eq = map(a, fit_synth, t_fit = t_eq),
    a_hat = map_dbl(irr, "a_hat"),
    shrink_irr = a_hat / a,
    shrink_eq = map_dbl(eq, "a_hat") / a,
    # exact attenuation for an exponential on an equal grid
    shrink_theory = 1 / ((abs_a * 2.5 / 2) / tanh(abs_a * 2.5 / 2)),
    fc_err_3 = map_dbl(irr, function(f) {
      x <- tail(f$traj, 1)
      100 * (x$Fitted - x$True) / x$True
    })
  )

synth_res |>
  select(direction, a, a_hat, shrink_irr, shrink_eq, shrink_theory,
         fc_err_3) |>
  kable(
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
      "Direction", "True a", "GMITS a (irregular grid)",
      "a_hat / a, irregular grid", "a_hat / a, equal grid",
      "Theory, equal grid", "Forecast error at step 3 (%)"
    ),
    caption = paste0(
      "GMITS parameter recovery on noise-free synthetic data ",
      "(b = 5, x0[1] = 8)"
    )
  ) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

```{r plot-synth-validate, fig.height = 8.5}
df_synth <- synth_res |>
  select(direction, abs_a, irr) |>
  mutate(traj = map(irr, "traj")) |>
  select(-irr) |>
  unnest(traj) |>
  mutate(
    rel_err = 100 * (Fitted - True) / True,
    direction = factor(direction, levels = c("Growth", "Decay")),
    speed = factor(paste0("|a| = ", abs_a))
  )

# Repeat the last fitted point in the forecast segment so the dashed
# forecast line starts where the solid fitted line ends
df_synth_plot <- bind_rows(
  df_synth |> filter(!Forecast) |> mutate(segment = "in-sample"),
  df_synth |>
    filter(Forecast | t == max(t_irr)) |>
    mutate(segment = "forecast")
) |>
  pivot_longer(c(True, Fitted), names_to = "type", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(segment = factor(segment, levels = c("in-sample", "forecast")))

synth_boundary <- geom_vline(
  xintercept = max(t_irr) + mean(diff(t_irr)) / 2,
  linetype = "dotted", color = "grey60"
)
synth_x <- expression("Time (days from " * t[0] * ")")
synth_xscale <- scale_x_continuous(limits = range(df_synth$t))
speed_cols <- c("|a| = 0.3" = "#86b6ef", "|a| = 0.4" = "#1c5cab")

p_values <- ggplot(
  df_synth_plot,
  aes(t, value, color = type, linetype = segment,
      group = interaction(type, segment))
) +
  synth_boundary +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(
    data = df_synth_plot |> filter(segment == "in-sample", type == "True"),
    size = 2
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(True = "black", Fitted = "steelblue"),
    name   = NULL
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c("in-sample" = "solid", "forecast" = "dashed"),
    name   = NULL
  ) +
  # one row per speed, one column per direction; each panel its own y
  facet_wrap(
    ~ speed + direction, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y",
    labeller = label_wrap_gen(multi_line = FALSE)
  ) +
  synth_xscale +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Period incidence")

p_error <- ggplot(
  df_synth |> filter(t > 0),
  aes(t, rel_err, color = speed)
) +
  synth_boundary +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey40") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = Forecast), size = 2.2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = speed_cols, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("FALSE" = 16, "TRUE" = 1),
    labels = c("FALSE" = "in-sample", "TRUE" = "forecast"),
    name   = NULL
  ) +
  # free_y keeps both panels' axes drawn (so they line up with the top
  # rows); the fixed limits keep one common scale
  facet_wrap(~ direction, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = range(c(0, df_synth$rel_err))) +
  synth_xscale +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = synth_x, y = "Relative error (%)")

p_values / p_error +
  plot_layout(heights = c(2, 1), guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "GMITS Synthetic Validation — Parameter Recovery",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Top: black = true ODE, blue = GMITS fit + 3-step forecast ",
      "(b = 5, x0[1] = 8, irregular grid).\n",
      "Bottom: (GMITS - true) / true, same y scale in both panels. ",
      "Dotted line = forecast boundary."
    )
  )
```

**Implementation note.** An earlier version of this page attributed
a much larger growth-phase underprediction to the background value;
most of it was an implementation error, corrected on 2026-10-13
([revision history](GMITS_Research.html#revision-history)). With the corrected regression GMITS
recovers every $a$ in the table to within
`r round(100 * max(abs(1 - synth_res$shrink_irr)), 1)`%.

**Remaining limitation — background-value bias.**
The residual gaps are the approximation bias of the GM(1,1) family. The
background value $z_{k} = \frac{1}{2}(x^{(1)}_{k} + x^{(1)}_{k-1})$
replaces the interval mean of $x^{(1)}$ by the mean of its endpoints.
When $x^{(1)}$ is curved this misstates the interval mean: in a growth
phase $x^{(1)}$ is convex and the endpoint mean *overstates* it; in a
decay phase $x^{(1)}$ is concave and the endpoint mean *understates* it.
In both cases the error is proportional to the distance of $x^{(1)}$
from its asymptote $b/a$, so the regression slope is attenuated and
$|\hat a|$ is pulled towards zero by the factor
$1 / [(h/2)\coth(h/2)]$ with $h = |a|\,\Delta t$, whatever the sign of
$a$: about 8% at $h = 1$ and under 0.1% at $h = 0.1$. Only the sign of
the resulting forecast error differs: a growth forecast grows too slowly
(underprediction) and a decay forecast decays too slowly
(overprediction).

The 2 × 2 design separates the three influences on this bias:

- **Speed:** a larger $|a|$ shrinks $|\hat a|$ more in both directions
  (equal grid: `r sprintf("%.3f", synth_res$shrink_eq[synth_res$a == 0.3])`
  at $|a| = 0.3$ vs.
  `r sprintf("%.3f", synth_res$shrink_eq[synth_res$a == 0.4])` at
  $|a| = 0.4$), and the forecast error grows with the horizon.
- **Direction:** on the equally spaced grid growth and decay are shrunk by
  exactly the same factor, which matches the theoretical value, so the
  direction of the trend on its own does not matter.
- **Spacing:** on the irregular grid (intervals 2, 2, 3, 3 days) growth is
  shrunk more than decay
  (`r sprintf("%.3f", synth_res$shrink_irr[synth_res$a == -0.3])` vs.
  `r sprintf("%.3f", synth_res$shrink_irr[synth_res$a == 0.3])` at
  $|a| = 0.3$). A growing $x^{(1)}$ changes most over the long late
  intervals, where the trapezoid error is largest, whereas a decaying
  $x^{(1)}$ changes most over the short early ones. Uneven reporting
  intervals therefore matter more when an outbreak is accelerating.

On a linear axis the decay fits look almost perfect only because the
counts approach zero; the relative-error panel shows the forecasts
drifting upwards by up to
`r round(max(synth_res$fc_err_3))`% after three steps.

This limitation is well-known in the grey system literature (Liu, 2025;
Liu & Deng, 2000) and is the motivation for optimising the background
coefficient $\alpha$ (replacing the fixed 0.5). That extension is outside
the scope of this study; the bias is reported here as an explicit boundary
condition for GMITS applicability: **the method is most reliable when
$|a| \times \overline{\Delta t}$ is small**, i.e., moderate growth rates
and short reporting intervals.

# Data

## 2011 Listeria Outbreak

Data extracted from https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/listeria/outbreaks/cantaloupes-jensen-farms/timeline.html
Sporadic foodborne transmission; illness-onset series (A files).
Snapshot `091211A` (Sep 12, 2011) is the **input**; `082712A` (Aug 27, 2012)
is the **ground truth** (final report).

```{r data-listeria}
wd <- "d:/Projects/RA/Listeria/data mdy"

read_snap <- function(fname) {
  read_csv(
    file.path(wd, fname),
    col_types = cols(Date = col_character(), Count = col_integer())
  ) |>
    mutate(
      Date = as.Date(Date),
      Snapshot = str_remove(fname, "\\.csv$")
    )
}

lst_input <- read_snap("091211A.csv") |> rename(Count_input = Count)
lst_gt    <- read_snap("082712A.csv") |> rename(Count_gt    = Count)

lst_combined <- full_join(
  lst_input |> select(Date, Count_input),
  lst_gt    |> select(Date, Count_gt),
  by = "Date"
) |>
  arrange(Date)

# Non-zero reporting days from input snapshot (091211A)
lst_nonzero <- lst_input |>
  filter(Count_input > 0) |>
  arrange(Date)

# First 6 non-zero days (n=6 primary)
lst_n6 <- lst_nonzero |> slice_head(n = 6)
# First 5 non-zero days
lst_n5 <- lst_nonzero |> slice_head(n = 5)
# First 4 non-zero days
lst_n4 <- lst_nonzero |> slice_head(n = 4)
```

```{r listeria-input-table}
lst_n6 |>
  mutate(delta_t = c(NA, diff(as.numeric(Date)))) |>
  kable(
    col.names = c("Date", "Count (input)", "Snapshot", "Δt (days)"),
    caption   = "Listeria input: first 6 non-zero reporting days (091211A)"
  ) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

# Early-Stage Forecasting

## Listeria (n = 4 / 5 / 6)

Three input sizes are compared. n = 6 is the primary scenario (maximum data
available from the Sep 12 snapshot before the forecast window). n = 4 and
n = 5 demonstrate sensitivity to input size.

```{r forecast-listeria}
n_ahead_l <- 4

run_listeria_fc <- function(df_n) {
  res_g  <- gmits_boot(df_n$Count_input, df_n$Date,
                       n_boot = 1000, n_ahead = n_ahead_l)
  res_er <- exp_reg(df_n$Count_input, df_n$Date, n_ahead = n_ahead_l)
  n_fit  <- nrow(df_n)
  dt_mean <- mean(diff(as.numeric(df_n$Date)))
  data.frame(
    Date     = c(df_n$Date,
                 df_n$Date[n_fit] + round(dt_mean * seq_len(n_ahead_l))),
    Point    = res_g$point,
    Lower    = res_g$lower,
    Upper    = res_g$upper,
    ExpReg   = c(res_er$x0_hat, res_er$x0_future),
    Forecast = c(rep(FALSE, n_fit), rep(TRUE, n_ahead_l)),
    n_label  = paste0("n = ", n_fit)
  )
}

df_lst_fc <- bind_rows(
  run_listeria_fc(lst_n4),
  run_listeria_fc(lst_n5),
  run_listeria_fc(lst_n6)
) |>
  mutate(n_label = factor(n_label, levels = c("n = 4", "n = 5", "n = 6")))
```

```{r plot-listeria-forecast}
gt_l <- lst_combined |>
  filter(!is.na(Count_gt)) |>
  select(Date, GT = Count_gt)

ggplot() +
  geom_col(
    data = gt_l |>
      filter(Date >= as.Date("2011-08-16"),
             Date <= as.Date("2011-09-10")),
    aes(Date, GT),
    fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = df_lst_fc,
    aes(Date, ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper, fill = n_label),
    alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = df_lst_fc,
    aes(Date, Point, color = n_label, linetype = Forecast),
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = df_lst_fc,
    aes(Date, ExpReg, color = n_label, linetype = Forecast),
    linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c("FALSE" = "solid", "TRUE" = "dashed"),
    labels = c("FALSE" = "in-sample", "TRUE" = "forecast"),
    guide  = guide_legend(title = NULL)
  ) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = "Input size") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette  = "Dark2", name = "Input size") +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%m/%d", date_breaks = "7 days") +
  facet_wrap(~ n_label, ncol = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Listeria — GMITS 4-Step Forecast by Input Size",
    subtitle = "Solid/dashed = GMITS; Dotted = exp. regression; Grey = final ground truth (082712A)",
    x = "Date", y = "Cases"
  )
```

# Right Truncation Sensitivity

The most recent observation in the n = 4 input (Aug 23, count = 1) may be
underreported due to reporting delay. We scale it by 1.5× and 2.0× and
compare the resulting 4-step forecasts.

```{r truncation-sensitivity}
adj_none <- lst_n4$Count_input
adj_1_5  <- truncation_adjust(lst_n4$Count_input, n_recent = 1, scale_factor = 1.5)
adj_2_0  <- truncation_adjust(lst_n4$Count_input, n_recent = 1, scale_factor = 2.0)

run_trunc <- function(counts, label) {
  res    <- gmits_boot(counts, lst_n4$Date, n_boot = 1000, n_ahead = n_ahead_l)
  n_fit  <- nrow(lst_n4)
  dt_mean <- mean(diff(as.numeric(lst_n4$Date)))
  data.frame(
    Date      = c(lst_n4$Date,
                  lst_n4$Date[n_fit] + round(dt_mean * seq_len(n_ahead_l))),
    Point     = res$point,
    Lower     = res$lower,
    Upper     = res$upper,
    Forecast  = c(rep(FALSE, n_fit), rep(TRUE, n_ahead_l)),
    Adjustment = label
  )
}

df_trunc <- bind_rows(
  run_trunc(adj_none, "No adjustment"),
  run_trunc(adj_1_5,  "Scale ×1.5"),
  run_trunc(adj_2_0,  "Scale ×2.0")
) |>
  mutate(Adjustment = factor(
    Adjustment,
    levels = c("No adjustment", "Scale ×1.5", "Scale ×2.0")
  ))
```

```{r plot-truncation}
ggplot() +
  geom_col(
    data = gt_l |>
      filter(Date >= as.Date("2011-08-16"),
             Date <= as.Date("2011-09-10")),
    aes(Date, GT),
    fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = df_trunc,
    aes(Date, ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper, fill = Adjustment),
    alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = df_trunc,
    aes(Date, Point, color = Adjustment, linetype = Forecast),
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c("FALSE" = "solid", "TRUE" = "dashed"),
    guide  = guide_legend(title = NULL)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("No adjustment" = "#1b9e77",
               "Scale ×1.5"   = "#d95f02",
               "Scale ×2.0"   = "#7570b3"),
    name = "Truncation adj."
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("No adjustment" = "#1b9e77",
               "Scale ×1.5"   = "#d95f02",
               "Scale ×2.0"   = "#7570b3"),
    name = "Truncation adj."
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%m/%d", date_breaks = "7 days") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Listeria n = 4 — Right Truncation Sensitivity",
    subtitle = "Point + 95% PI under three adjustments; Grey = final ground truth",
    x = "Date", y = "Cases"
  )
```

# Out-of-Sample Error Summary

Ground truth: `082712A` at all 4 forecast steps (n = 6 input scenario).

```{r error-summary}
fc_n6 <- df_lst_fc |>
  filter(n_label == "n = 6", Forecast)

lst_gt_fc <- lst_combined |>
  filter(Date %in% fc_n6$Date) |>
  select(Date, Count_gt)

lst_err <- fc_n6 |>
  left_join(lst_gt_fc, by = "Date") |>
  filter(!is.na(Count_gt))

data.frame(
  Model    = c("GMITS", "Exp. Reg."),
  n_input  = c(6L, 6L),
  n_steps  = c(nrow(lst_err), nrow(lst_err)),
  MAE_oos  = c(
    mae(lst_err$Count_gt, lst_err$Point),
    mae(lst_err$Count_gt, lst_err$ExpReg)
  ),
  MAPE_oos = c(
    mape(lst_err$Count_gt, lst_err$Point),
    mape(lst_err$Count_gt, lst_err$ExpReg)
  )
) |>
  kable(
    digits    = 2,
    col.names = c("Model", "n input", "Steps verified",
                  "MAE (oos)", "MAPE % (oos)"),
    caption   = "Out-of-sample error: GMITS vs. exponential regression (Listeria, n = 6)"
  ) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```
